strings.scrini-ne-montre-pas-de-publicite-et-ne: Scrini doesn't show ads and doesn't sell your data. Your library belongs to you — you can export it as a spreadsheet, or delete your account and everything in it.
strings.ce-produit-utilise-l-api-tmdb-mais-n-est: This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
strings.quand-sort-le-prochain-episode-scrini: When does the next episode come out? — Scrini
strings.l-agenda-des-diffusions-a-venir-de-tes: A calendar of upcoming air dates for your TV shows, week by week, with each show's release schedule, and a notification on the morning of release day — no emails to sort through.
strings.quand-sort-le-prochain-episode: When does the next episode come out?
strings.l-agenda-des-diffusions-a-venir-semaine: A calendar of upcoming air dates, week by week, and an alert on the morning of release day.
strings.chercher-une-date-de-diffusion-c-est: Looking up an air date means opening a search engine, landing on an article from last year, then on a forum talking about a different season. Scrini answers the question for the shows you already follow.
strings.l-application-rassemble-les-diffusions-a: The app gathers the upcoming air dates of your shows and lays them out week by week. You're not hunting for a date: you look at what's coming and you know what the next two weeks look like.
strings.l-agenda-indique-aussi-le-rythme-de: The calendar also shows each show's release schedule. That's what's most often missing elsewhere, and what costs you the most when you don't know it: a season can switch from weekly episodes to dropping all at once, or take a two-month break in the middle. Seeing the schedule means understanding why nothing has come out for three weeks, without having to check whether you missed something.
strings.le-matin-d-une-sortie-une-notification: On the morning of a release, a notification shows up on your device. No extra email to sort through, no feed to keep an eye on: the information reaches you on the day it's useful, and not before.
strings.si-elles-t-encombrent-elles-se-coupent: If they get in your way, you can turn them all off in one go. That's on purpose: an app that makes unsubscribing a pain ends up uninstalled, which does nobody any good.
strings.ce-que-l-accueil-peut-afficher: What the home screen can show
strings.les-sorties-attendues-sont-l-une-des: Upcoming releases are one of the home screen rows, and you choose which rows appear and in what order. Depending on how you set it up, the app opens on your lists, on the releases you're waiting for, on what's trending today, on series currently airing, or on movies now in theaters in your country. If the calendar is what you care about, it can be the first thing you see.
strings.les-calendriers-de-diffusion-proviennent: Air schedules come from The Movie Database, a database maintained by a community of contributors. It's good, and it isn't infallible: a date that's announced and then moved by a network sometimes takes a day or two to be corrected there, and niche shows are less well kept up than big productions. The app shows what the database contains — no more, no better.

strings.savoir-ou-on-en-est-dans-ses-series: Keep track of where you are in your TV shows

strings.pourquoi-ils-se-filtrent-a-part: — why it has its own filter.
strings.savoir-ou-on-en-est-dans-ses-series-scri: Keep track of where you are in your TV shows — Scrini
strings.reprendre-une-serie-six-mois-plus-tard: Pick a show back up six months later without playing three random episodes: an episode tracker where you check off what you've watched, find the next one, and see progress that only counts what has actually aired.
strings.savoir-ou-on-en-est-dans-ses-series-2: Keep track of where you are in your TV shows
strings.cocher-les-episodes-vus-retrouver-le: Check off the episodes you've watched, find the next one, and see progress that only counts what has actually aired.
strings.une-serie-interrompue-en-avril-reprise-e: You stopped a show in April and pick it back up in October: you play a random episode, realize you've already seen it, try another one. Here's how Scrini saves you that wasted fifteen minutes.
strings.cocher-plutot-que-se-souvenir: Check it off instead of remembering
strings.le-principe-tient-en-un-geste-tu-coches: It all comes down to one gesture: you check off the episodes you've watched as you go. The app doesn't guess anything, doesn't read what you're watching and doesn't connect to any platform — it records what you tell it, and that's it. In return, the information is accurate, even when you've watched on three different services or at someone else's place.
strings.sur-l-accueil-chaque-serie-en-cours: On the home screen, each series in progress shows you the next episode: the one you need to play, not the one that aired this week. The question “wait, where was I?” goes away because it's already answered when you open the app.
strings.une-progression-qui-ne-compte-pas-les: Progress that doesn't count upcoming episodes
strings.c-est-un-detail-dont-on-ne-mesure-l: It's one of those details you only appreciate once you have it. When a season is still airing, most trackers show your progress against the announced total: you've watched the six episodes out of ten that are out, so you're told 60% and an unfinished season. That's wrong — you're caught up.
strings.scrini-ne-compte-que-les-episodes: Scrini only counts episodes that have actually aired. A series you follow week by week therefore shows as finished as long as there's nothing new, and goes back to behind the day a new episode drops. The difference between “I have four episodes left” and “there aren't any yet” changes what you do with your evening.
strings.une-fois-l-episode-identifie-reste-a: Once you know which episode is next, you still need to know where it's streaming. Each title shows the platforms that offer it in the country or region set in the app, along with its cast. This information comes from JustWatch, via TMDB: it's only as good as their data, and an exclusive that changes hands can take a few days to show up there.
strings.tout-ce-que-tu-coches-s-exporte-au-forma: Everything you check off can be exported as a spreadsheet from “Export my data” in Settings, anytime, with no request to make and no waiting. That's the guarantee that matters when you trust an app with years of viewing: you can leave with it. The rest — what's kept, where, and for how long — is described in the
strings.l-agenda-des-diffusions-et-les-alertes: — the air date calendar and alerts.
strings.suivre-ses-animes-scrini: Anime tracker: track your anime — Scrini
strings.les-animes-ne-sont-ni-des-films-ni-des: Anime isn't movies and it isn't TV shows: in Scrini it has its own filter, combines with genre, rating and decades, and you track it episode by episode like everything else.
strings.un-filtre-a-part-cumulable-avec-le-genre: Its own filter, which combines with genre, rating and decades, in search as well as in your lists.
strings.ranges-parmi-les-series-les-animes-se: Filed in with TV shows, anime gets lost: three hundred episodes on one side, six on the other, and a list where you can't find anything anymore. Scrini treats anime as the category it is.
strings.un-filtre-a-part-parce-que-ce-sont-des: Its own filter, because it's its own thing
strings.les-animes-ne-sont-ni-des-films-ni-des-2: Anime isn't movies and it isn't TV shows, and mixing them makes a library impossible to read. In Scrini, anime has its own filter — in search as well as in your own lists. So you can look at just your anime, or set it aside while you decide between two shows.
strings.le-filtre-anime-se-combine-avec-les: The anime filter combines with the others instead of replacing them: genre, minimum rating, decades, upcoming releases. “Sci-fi anime from the 1990s above a certain rating” is a question you ask in a few taps, and the same combination works on your list just like on the catalog.
strings.les-decennies-meritent-une-mention-c-est: Decades deserve a special mention: it's the filter that makes searching for anime bearable, because the medium has very distinct eras, and sorting by relevance alone always surfaces the same recent titles.
strings.pour-le-reste-un-anime-se-suit-comme-une: Beyond that, you track an anime just like a series: you check off the episodes you've watched, the home screen shows you the next one, and progress only counts what has actually aired — which matters all the more for a season that's being simulcast. Upcoming episodes show up in
strings.avec-une-notification-le-matin-de-la: , with a notification on the morning of release day.
strings.ce-qu-il-faut-savoir-sur-les-donnees: What to know about the data
strings.les-fiches-viennent-de-the-movie-databas: Title pages come from The Movie Database, which isn't a database specialized in Japanese animation. In practice, well-known titles are well kept up there, but the way a long-running series is split into seasons can differ from the one used by specialized databases, and fine distinctions — season, arc, part — aren't always reflected. Better to know that before pouring in a list of two hundred titles.
strings.les-plateformes-qui-proposent-chaque: The platforms offering each title in the country or region set in the app are shown when the information exists, based on JustWatch data provided through TMDB.

strings.une-application-qui-sert-a-suivre-les: An app for tracking the movies, TV shows and anime you watch: check off the episodes you've seen, know where you are in every season, and get a heads-up on upcoming releases. It doesn't stream any content.
strings.oui-elle-est-gratuite-sans-publicite-san: Yes. It's free, with no ads, no tracking and no selling of your data.
strings.sur-quels-appareils-scrini-fonctionne-t: What devices does Scrini work on?
strings.sur-android-7-et-versions-ulterieures-su: Android 7 and later, iPhone with iOS 15 or later, and any browser at https://app.scrini.fr — on a computer or a phone, with nothing to install.
strings.peut-on-utiliser-scrini-sur-ordinateur: Can I use Scrini on a computer?
strings.oui-sur-https-app-scrini-fr-c-est-la-mem: Yes, at https://app.scrini.fr: it's the same app, opened in your browser, with the same account and the same library as on your phone. Nothing to install. Release alerts, though, are still a job for the mobile app, which schedules them with your phone's system.
strings.peut-on-regarder-des-films-ou-des-series: Can I watch movies or TV shows in Scrini?
strings.non-scrini-n-heberge-ne-diffuse-et-ne-li: Not the movies or series themselves: Scrini doesn't host or stream any of them. It shows which platforms offer each title in the country or region set in the app, and you open the one you subscribe to. Only trailers play inside the app, in YouTube's player.
strings.faut-il-creer-un-compte-pour-utiliser: Do I need an account to use Scrini?
strings.oui-c-est-ce-qui-rattache-ta-bibliothequ: To track your movies and series, yes: that's what ties your library to you rather than to a device, and gives it back to you when you switch phones. You sign in with a code sent to your email, or with Google or Apple. Signing in with a code only shares your email address, whereas Google and Apple also pass along your name and the address of your profile picture — which the app neither reads nor displays. To browse the home screen, search and title pages, “Continue without an account” is enough.
strings.ton-adresse-email-les-titres-que-tu-suis: Your email address, the titles you track along with their list, your rating, your comments and your watch dates, your episode-by-episode progress, your home screen display settings, the app's language and the regions chosen for the catalog and theaters. When something breaks, a technical log is kept for thirty days, long enough to figure out what went wrong. Nothing else: no audience measurement, no ad trackers, no location data, no access to your contacts, files or camera. The details are in the privacy policy.
strings.les-notifications-de-scrini-passent-elle: Do Scrini's notifications go through a third-party service?
strings.non-les-alertes-de-sortie-sont: No. Release alerts are scheduled locally by the app with your phone's system: no token or identifier is sent to any outside notification service.
strings.d-ou-viennent-les-informations-sur-les: Where does Scrini's movie and TV show info come from?
strings.de-the-movie-database-pour-les-fiches-et: From The Movie Database for title pages and air schedules, and from JustWatch via TMDB for streaming availability. These are community-maintained databases: when a network moves a date, it can take a day or two to be corrected there.
strings.puis-je-recuperer-ma-liste-si-je-quitte: Can I get my list back if I leave Scrini?
strings.oui-a-tout-moment-et-sans-rien-demander-: Yes, anytime, without having to ask: the spreadsheet export is in the app, under “Export my data” in Settings.
strings.comment-supprimer-son-compte-scrini: How do I delete my Scrini account?
strings.depuis-l-application-en-trois-gestes-ou: From the app in three taps, or from the account deletion page. Deletion is permanent and immediate, and takes all of the account's data with it.
strings.les-animes-sont-ils-geres-comme-les-seri: Is anime handled the same way as TV shows?
strings.non-et-c-est-voulu-ils-se-filtrent-a-par: No, and that's on purpose: anime has its own filter, in search as well as in your lists, because mixing it in makes a library impossible to read. The filter combines with genre, minimum rating and decades.

strings.scrini-enregistre-les-films-et-les-serie: Scrini stores the movies and TV shows you track, and what it needs to work. No audience measurement, no ad trackers, no selling of your data. This page describes what is kept, where, and how to make it disappear.

strings.aucun-usage-de-notre-cote-ces: We don't use them. This information comes with the sign-in and is kept as is by the authentication service: the app doesn't read it, doesn't display it anywhere and doesn't pass it on to anyone.
strings.titres-suivis-film-ou-serie-liste-a-voir: Tracked titles: movie or series, list (to watch, in progress, watched, dropped), rating out of 10, comment, date watched, personal categories

strings.progression-par-episode-saison-numero: Episode progress: season, number, date watched
strings.savoir-ou-tu-en-es-dans-une-serie-et-te: To know where you are in a series and suggest the next episode.
strings.tes-notes-personnelles-visibles-de-toi: Your personal notes, visible only to you.
strings.reglages-de-l-ecran-d-accueil-les-rangee: Home screen settings: the rows you keep, and their order
strings.retrouver-ton-accueil-tel-que-tu-l-as: To bring back your home screen just as you set it up, from one device to another. They say nothing about what you watch.
strings.afficher-l-application-les-titres-et-les: To show the app, titles and synopses in your language on all your devices. It's taken from your device the first time you sign in, and you can change it in the settings.
strings.la-base-legale-de-ces-traitements-est-l: The legal basis for this processing is the
strings.que-tu-demandes-en-creant-un-compte-sans: you request by creating an account. Without this data, the app has no purpose.
strings.quand-une-panne-survient-et-que-l: When something breaks and the app recovers on its own — a data source that's unavailable, a list that won't load — it logs a trace of it:
strings.l-endroit-concerne-le-message-d-erreur-l: where it happened, the error message, the app version and the operating system
strings.sans-quoi-une-panne-permanente-serait: . Otherwise, a permanent outage would be impossible to tell apart from normal operation.
strings.ces-enregistrements-sont-rattaches-a-ton: These records are linked to your account, so we can tell an outage that affects one person from one that affects everyone. They are
strings.et-immediatement-a-la-suppression-du: , and immediately when the account is deleted. Any web addresses quoted in an error message have their parameters stripped before being written: a failed search doesn't leave behind what you typed.
strings.ce-n-est-ni-une-mesure-d-audience-ni-un: This is neither audience measurement nor usage tracking: nothing is logged when everything works. The legal basis is our
strings.les-fiches-de-films-et-de-series-passent: Movie and TV show pages go through a relay server (see TMDB below). So that a single account can't use up everyone's access, this relay counts,
strings.par-compte-et-par-fenetre-de-quelques: per account and per window of a few minutes
strings.le-nombre-de-requetes-qu-il-transmet-un: , the number of requests it forwards — a number, nothing about their content. This count is
strings.a-garder-le-service-disponible-pour-tous: in keeping the service available to everyone.
strings.le-theme-choisi-l-activation-des-alertes: Your chosen theme, whether release alerts are turned on, and cached images stay on the device. Notifications are
strings.elles-sont-programmees-par-l-application: : the app schedules them with the system, without any token or identifier being sent to a third-party notification service.
strings.aucune-mesure-d-audience-aucun-outil-d: No audience measurement, no behavioral analytics tools.
strings.aucun-traceur-ni-identifiant-publicitair: No trackers or advertising identifiers on our part. Only Google may store information on your device, when you start a trailer or open the web version — see below.
strings.aucun-acces-a-tes-contacts-a-tes-fichier: No access to your contacts, your files or your camera.
strings.la-base-de-donnees-et-le-service-d: The database and the authentication service are hosted by
strings.ta-bibliotheque-et-ton-compte-sont: region: your library and your account are stored on servers located in France. Supabase is an American company, whose data infrastructure here is in Europe.
strings.seul-l-acheminement-des-emails-de: Some third-party services, described below, do receive data and may process it outside the European Union: the delivery of sign-in emails, Google or Apple sign-in if you choose it, posters and images, loaded from TMDB's servers, and Google services (YouTube trailers, the web version).
strings.chaque-compte-est-cloisonne-au-niveau-de: Each account is isolated at the database level itself: the server's security rules only allow a row to be read and written by the account that created it.
strings.les-fiches-de-films-et-de-series: Movie and TV show pages come from TMDB. Your requests go through a relay server that queries TMDB
strings.tmdb-recoit-la-recherche-jamais-l: : TMDB receives the search, never who made it. Streaming availability comes from JustWatch, via TMDB. This app uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
strings.les-codes-de-connexion-te-sont-envoyes-p: Sign-in codes are sent to you by
strings.societe-americaine-qui-recoit-a-cette: , an American company, which receives your email address and the code for that purpose. It has no access to your library or to the rest of your data.
strings.connexion-google-ou-apple: Signing in with Google or Apple
strings.si-tu-choisis-de-te-connecter-avec-un: If you choose to sign in with a Google or Apple account, that provider knows you're signing in to Scrini and sends us your email address, your name and — for Google — the address of your profile picture. None of the app's features ask for the last two. They're kept with your account, without being read or displayed. We never receive your password or the contents of your account with them. Signing in with a code sent by email avoids this step entirely.
strings.combien-de-temps-tes-donnees-sont: How long your data is kept
strings.aussi-longtemps-que-ton-compte-existe-a: For as long as your account exists, with two exceptions: the error reports described above delete themselves after thirty days, and the catalog request count every night. There is no archiving: when the account is deleted, all the data described above is erased from the database, with no copy kept.
strings.une-fiche-fausse-une-affiche-manquante: A wrong title page, a missing poster, an incorrect release date: this data comes from the TMDB catalog and gets fixed on their end, at
strings.la-correction-remonte-ensuite-dans-scrin: . The fix then makes its way into Scrini.
strings.un-bug-un-contenu-inapproprie-une-donnee: A bug, inappropriate content, personal data shown by mistake or a security flaw: write to
strings.chaque-signalement-recoit-une-reponse: . Every report gets a reply within one month, and security reports are handled first.
strings.le-rgpd-te-donne-un-droit-d-acces-de: The GDPR gives you the right of access, rectification, erasure, portability and objection. In practice:
strings.toutes-tes-donnees-sont-visibles-et: : all your data is visible and editable right in the app.
strings.la-bibliotheque-s-exporte-au-format: : your library can be exported as a spreadsheet from the app, without going through us.
strings.pour-toute-autre-demande-a-l-adresse-de: for any other request, at the contact address given above. Reply within one month.

strings.l-application-n-est-pas-destinee-aux: The app is not intended for children under 13 and does not knowingly ask them for any data.
strings.toute-evolution-de-cette-politique-sera: Any change to this policy will be published on this page, with its update date. A change affecting the kind of data collected will be announced in the app.
strings.comment-supprimer-ton-compte-scrini-et: How to delete your Scrini account and all its data, from the app or by email.
strings.comment-supprimer-ton-compte-scrini-et-2: How to delete your Scrini account and all its data.
strings.c-est-le-chemin-le-plus-rapide-et-il-n-a: It's the fastest way, and you don't need anyone's help:
strings.confirme-la-suppression-est-immediate-et: Confirm. Deletion is immediate and permanent.
strings.pense-a-exporter-ta-bibliotheque-en: If you want to keep your library, remember to export it as a spreadsheet first.
strings.si-tu-n-as-plus-l-application-installee: If you no longer have the app installed, write to us from your account's email address. Your request will be handled within thirty days.
strings.ton-compte-et-ton-adresse-email: Your account and your email address.
strings.ta-bibliotheque-titres-suivis-statuts: Your library: tracked titles, statuses, checked episodes, ratings, comments and lists.
strings.tes-preferences-et-tes-alertes-de-sortie: Your preferences and your release alerts.
strings.les-signalements-d-erreur-rattaches-a-to: Error reports linked to your account.
strings.tout-part-en-meme-temps-rien-n-est: Everything goes at once: nothing is kept, no copy, no retention period. Deletion can't be undone — a new account starts from scratch.
strings.p-ecris-a-a-href-mailto-contact-scrini-f: Write to contact@scrini.fr. See also the privacy policy.
strings.p-les-bandes-annonces-sont-lues-dans-le: Trailers play in YouTube's embedded player, a Google service, through the YouTube API Services. The player only loads when you start a trailer: until then, YouTube receives nothing. As soon as you start one, Google receives the requested video, your IP address, the language chosen in Scrini and technical information about your browser or phone, and may store or read information on your device (cookies, local storage), even in privacy-enhanced mode. YouTube may also show ads in its player. Scrini passes on neither your identity nor your library. By starting a trailer, you agree to the YouTube Terms of Service; what Google does with this data is governed by its Privacy Policy. To keep anything from reaching it, simply don't start a trailer.
strings.p-sur-la-version-web-app-scrini-fr-la: On the web version (app.scrini.fr), Google's sign-in script is loaded from Google's servers as soon as the app opens, whether or not you sign in with Google. Google then receives your IP address and information about your browser; if you are already signed in to a Google account in that browser, it can also read its own cookies and learn that you opened Scrini. The web version's rendering engine and its fonts are also downloaded from Google's servers, which receive your IP address in the process. The Android and iOS apps make none of these calls. This processing is governed by Google's Privacy Policy.

strings.p-les-fiches-affiches-et-images-des: Movie and series details, posters and images come from The Movie Database (TMDB). This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.

strings.regions-du-catalogue-et-du-cinema: Catalog and theater regions (one country each)
strings.montrer-ce-qui-sort-ce-qui-passe-en-sall: Show what's coming out and what's playing in theaters in your country, and where to watch each title. They're set in Settings, and follow your device's country by default.
strings.p-continuer-sans-compte-ouvre-une-sessio: “Continue without an account” opens an anonymous session, which carries no email address or name. It's only used to browse the catalog, and the request count described above applies to it; nothing else is stored. An anonymous session inactive for thirty days is deleted.
strings.p-les-affiches-et-les-images-elles-sont: Posters and images, however, are loaded directly from TMDB's image servers, which receive your IP address in the process — but neither your account nor your library.
